method: single-listener blind per-case A/B preference; not MOS

conditions.candidate: direct dense russtress 0.1.4 output converted to U+0301 without Gemini

cases.interpretation: Both target homograph positions were correct, so this case primarily probes the perceptual effect of dense ordinary-word stress marks.

decision: Reject direct russtress as an autonomous production normalizer because contextual stress errors dominated two of three cases. Do not conclude that dense marking always harms prosody: the listener preferred dense russtress in the positive-control strelki case. Run a separate longer-prose A/B with independently verified correct stresses to isolate prosody and listening fatigue from pronunciation accuracy.
